findings.title: Two students find one undescribed trace while the GM's describe window is open: a second window opens from the record before the first answer, and confirming it wipes the first description on the trace and on the first finder's copy (closing it gives the second finder a copy under another name with no words)
findings.where: scripts/observe.mjs:1026-1051 (createFind reads the trace's public record once, before the window, and writes and mints from that reading after it); scripts/observe.mjs:1179-1281 (describeFind's prefill); scripts/remnants.mjs:1428-1457 (setRemnantPublic writes the patch as given, empty strings included)
findings.what_happens: resolveObserve runs on the primary for each player's observe.resolve; the bridge row has no queue (bridge-guards.mjs:1826), so two resolves run side by side. createFind reads `stored` (line 1026), and for a trace nobody has named opens describeFind and waits for the GM. A second student's successful Observe of the same trace, resolved while that window stands, reads the same empty record and opens a second window, prefilled with the fallback name and two empty boxes. The GM answers the first: the trace takes its name, words and reading. The second call still holds `described = null`: confirmed as drawn, it writes { name: fallback, playerText: "", analyzedText: "" } over them (1042-1046), and setRemnantPublic sends all three changed fields to the first finder's copy (truth-bullets.mjs:925-952). Closed instead, it writes nothing but mints the second copy from the stale `pub = stored` (1037, 1059-1063): the fallback name and no description, which nothing reconciles later.
findings.failure_scenario: Two players sweep the body's room within the half minute the GM takes to type 'Bloody knife' and its description; the GM presses the second window's button and both Truth Bullets now read 'Something found in the Kitchen' with no words, or closes it and the two players hold one object under two names.
findings.expected: One trace, one description, asked once: the comment in createFind (observe.mjs:987-1003) says two names for one object is the false contradiction the mechanism exists to prevent, and that later observers read the same words 'without the GM being asked again'. A find resolved while the trace is being described should wait for that answer, or re-read the record after its own window and treat words written meanwhile as the description.
findings.fix_sketch: Queue createFind's describe-and-write per trace (serialWrite on the trace's key) or re-read remnantPublicById after describeFind and skip the write and the stale `pub` when a name arrived meanwhile.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a guard across characters: `describing` (observe.mjs:770) is keyed by Observe key and read per character (pendingTracesOf, 329-333); the H84 re-check and serialWrite at mint are per character (1104, observeFindKey); observe.resolve has no `queue` in bridge-table.mjs:123-138, and judge runs unqueued work at once (bridge-guards.mjs:1826). drpgWindow is given no id, so the second window is not folded into the first. setRemnantPublic writes the named fields as given and reports each as changed when it differs from before (remnants.mjs:1438-1456). The General reading picks the first of a ranked list (observe.mjs:281-282), so two students who hold no copy are aimed at the same trace. No recorded decision found for two finders at once (git grep describeFind in docs/dev, the handbooks and AUDIT).
findings.tests_near: tier 2 'H84-02: one trace, one Truth Bullet per character ...' (tests-tier2.mjs:77641) drives two Observes of one character; R1120 (tier 0) reads the prefill of one window; E51-T12/T13 read a window closed unanswered. None resolves two characters' finds of one undescribed trace with the first window still open.
findings.live_check: On a real table or the harness: place one hand-made trace with no name, have two players each roll a General Observe that succeeds; leave the first describe window open until the second appears, answer the first with a name and words, then confirm the second untouched. Read both bullets' names and descriptions and the trace's row on the dashboard.

findings.title: Observe's target step answers, before anything is paid, whether the room holds a trace the character has not copied - and, asked as 'non-obvious', a secret project they are not in on
findings.where: scripts/bridge-table.mjs:108-115 (observe.target: knownSender, notSpectator, owns - no payment, no phase); scripts/bridge-runs-acts.mjs:51-63 (the ruling is replied whole); scripts/observe.mjs:201-225 (ok false with reason "none", or a key); scripts/action-observe.mjs:77-97 (the ask comes before spendAction, and a closed roll window refunds)
findings.what_happens: For a General, Non-obvious or Follow-my-traces Observe the player's browser asks observe.target first and pays only after the answer. The primary answers { ok: true, key } when rankForObserve leaves a candidate, { ok: false, reason: "none" } when it leaves none, and for 'nonObvious' { ok: true } also when the room holds nothing but a secret project the asker's account is not in on. The reply reaches the browser before the action is spent; closing the roll window that follows hands the action back (action-observe.mjs:86-89, action-pipeline.mjs:975-978). A console that sends observe.target alone pays nothing at all. Each asked room costs the GM a pending row and a console log line, and tells the asker one fact the file's own header lists as what the observer must not know.
findings.failure_scenario: A player with the browser's network tab open presses Observe, General in every room they walk through, reads ok true or false in the socket frame and closes the roll window: no action spent, and they know which rooms somebody left a trace in; 'general' false beside 'nonObvious' true says a secret project is being built there.
findings.expected: observe.mjs:14-24: which Remnants are in the room is 'something the observer must not know', and 'The player is told the outcome, never the difficulty'. The answer to the target step should not differ between a room with something and a room with nothing until the action is paid (a key either way, the empty room ruled at the resolve), or the target should be given only against a payment the GM saw.
findings.fix_sketch: Answer { ok: true, key } for every legal declaration and decide 'nothing here' when the paid roll is resolved, or claim the action's payment ticket in observe.target as askToFrisk does.
findings.refutation_tried: Read the row's guards and the run: nothing asks for a payment, a roll or a phase; chooseObserveTarget has no check of its own beyond the actor and the room (observe.mjs:181-191). bridge-asks.mjs:817-826 says the answer 'says only whether there is something to look at' - that is the fact in question. The UI no longer shows the difference before the dice (ROLL-11, action-observe.mjs:91-94), but the reply is on the wire. The trust model's list of what stays open (the rule file trust-model.md, 'What stays open') does not name it, and no decision was found in docs/dev or AUDIT (git grep observe.target).
findings.tests_near: 30-security.mjs:1531-1541: another player's request for Botan's key is refused for ownership, and the control - the owner's own request, with nothing paid - mints a key; so the unpaid answer is the pinned behaviour of the legal road, and nothing reads what it tells. 33-bridge-paths.mjs:207 the same.
findings.live_check: As a player, in a room with one uncopied trace and in an empty one: `const B = await import('/modules/danganronpa-rpg/scripts/gm-bridge.mjs'); await B.requestObserveTarget({ actorId: <own>, declaration: 'general' })` - read ok and reason in both, and the actions before and after.

findings.where: scripts/frisk.mjs:409-426 (performFrisk reads res only for its card's text); scripts/frisk.mjs:305-307 (friskPerson refuses on the one gate before either total is used); against scripts/palm.mjs:378-391 and 232-246 (palmBack on the gate's codes and on noGm) and scripts/frisk.mjs:1255-1256 (the open road)
findings.what_happens: performFrisk pays the action, throws Shadow and Hand in two roll windows, then asks action.friskUnseen. friskPerson asks personActionRefusal first: the target has walked out, an Eclipse or a Class Trial has begun, the asker now knows the target dead. The refusal comes back with one of the gate's codes, the bridge says it, and performFrisk goes on to noteRollContext, report and drpgActionResolved with nothing handed back. The same refusal of a Steal or a Plant is read in performPalm and the action returned by its receipt (palm.mjs:390-391), as is a request no GM was left to take (nobodyTook).
findings.failure_scenario: A student starts an unseen Frisk; while the two roll windows are open the target's token leaves the room. The GM refuses ('not there'), the player reads the refusal and a roll card, and the action is gone - the same thing as a Steal would have come back.
findings.expected: docs/handbooks/player-handbook.en.md:463, in the section that covers all three directions of Palm: 'A Palm refused before its dice are read (the target walked out, a Class Trial began) gives you its action back'; the owner's Q3 of 18.10.2026 quoted in palm.mjs:379-380 ('a refusal before the rolls are read refunds'), applied to Find Stash (action-analyze.mjs:361-369) and Find Passage (419-426) since.
findings.fix_sketch: In performFrisk, hand the action back with abort(actor, paid) on noGm and on a refusal whose code is one of TRANSFER_REFUSED, as performPalm does, and skip the report.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for the refund on another road: requestFriskUnseen (bridge-asks.mjs:1177-1188) only says the refusal; handleFriskUnseen passes it on (bridge-runs-acts.mjs:710-718); nothing on the GM returns an action (the comment at frisk.mjs:458-461 says the primary cannot). Looked for a decision that an unseen Frisk stays paid: none in the handbooks, the release notes or docs/dev; frisk.mjs:383-385 speaks only of a closed roll window (ROLL-05). The gate's refusal precedes any use of the totals (305-313), which is the case Q3 names.
findings.tests_near: tier 2 'an unseen Frisk is judged on the primary from a player's two drawn rolls (A11-5, A11-15)' (tests-tier2.mjs:12520) and 'a death the table knows is no Frisk's on any road' (13438) call friskPerson and read its cards and its refusal, not the searcher's actions afterwards; 33-bridge-paths C reads a Frisk with no GM before the price. The Palm refund's tests (E14 part 1) drive Steal and Plant.

findings.title: A GM's retype of a found Key or Final Remnant is written onto every copy nobody analysed: the copy shows the corrected kind, can no longer be analysed and never gets its reading, yet reads as 'read' to every road that asks
findings.where: scripts/truth-bullets.mjs:1010-1021 and 1025-1028 (propagateVerdicts: the kind onto every copy `isIdentified`); scripts/truth-bullets.mjs:309-313 (a Key showing its kind is identified), 369-373 (hasReading), 472-483 (isAnalysable); reached from scripts/investigation.mjs:2515-2523 through scripts/remnants.mjs:2243-2246
findings.what_happens: A Key or a Final copy shows its kind from pickup with `analyzed` false (createTruthBullet, 697-702, 732), so the GMs hold it identified. When a GM corrects the trace's kind on the Traces tab - the planner even has a status for it, 'keyRetyped' (investigation.mjs:857) - propagateVerdicts writes shownType = the new kind on that copy. Now shownType is e.g. 'prep' and analyzed is false: isAnalysable answers false (478), so neither the sheet nor resolveAnalyze (analyze.mjs:93) lets its holder analyse it, and its analyzedText stays empty; hasReading answers true (not Key, not Final), so the next rewrite of the reading is published onto it (propagateRemnantPublic, 939) and a copy handed over with its analysis is born with the reading (handover.mjs:310-311 into createTruthBullet's `read`, 702). The rule the function states for a Neutral copy - a correction must not hand the answer to its holder - is not held for a copy that was showing Key.
findings.failure_scenario: Two students hold an unanalysed Key Truth Bullet; the GM retypes its Remnant to Cleanup on the dashboard. Both bullets now read Cleanup without a Head roll, the Analyze button no longer offers them, and what analysis reveals never reaches either sheet.
findings.expected: truth-bullets.mjs:968-970: 'an unanalysed copy is showing "Neutral" and must go on showing it, or a GM's correction would hand the answer to everybody holding one', and 540-557: every trace has a description and a description after Analyze, bought by a roll. A copy that showed only a self-evident kind should fall back to what an unread copy of the new kind shows (Neutral for an analysable kind) and stay analysable.
findings.fix_sketch: In propagateVerdicts write the kind onto the item only where the copy has its reading (hasReading(held)); for a copy identified by a self-evident kind alone write unanalysedType(type).
findings.refutation_tried: Traced setRemnantFlags to propagateVerdicts with the Save's type (remnants.mjs:2217, 2243-2246) and read every reader of the resulting state (isAnalysable, hasReading, analysableBullets, resolveAnalyze's refusal, createTruthBullet's `read`). The opposite direction (a Neutral copy retyped to Key) leaves the copy Neutral and analysable, which is consistent. Looked for a test or a decision on a retyped Key's copies: the tier-2 tests below read analysed or Neutral copies and the planner's line.
findings.tests_near: tier 2 'a tie verdict or a kind reaches the copy's answer key and its flag if identified' (tests-tier2.mjs:35422) corrects a kind on a fixture of an analysed and a Neutral copy; 'a planned Key Remnant retyped on the dashboard is said to be no longer a Key Remnant and not gone' (30406) reads the planner's status, not the copies.

findings.where: scripts/investigation.mjs:2159 (the tooltip), 2149-2165 (offerFinalOnClose), 2430-2437 (the close, then the reopen with `said` alone), 1004-1027 (caseFinalPanel draws every field empty); lang/en.json:2123, lang/pl.json:2213

'Not now' carries the tooltip DRPG.Tips.Case.keepForLaterTooltip. offerFinalOnClose then returns false and nothing reads the form again: after the X, Escape or Close the window is gone; after a footer button the dashboard is opened anew by openInvestigationDashboard({ said }), whose Final form is drawn with empty values. saveDrawnForm writes the traces', the Key slots' and the schema's fields only (readCaseFields has no Final field, by its own comment at 1644-1648).
findings.evidence:
close: { role: "close", action: "later", label: L("DRPG.CaseRealize.notNow"), tooltip: tipText("DRPG.Tips.Case.keepForLaterTooltip") }, default: "place" },
...
if (answer !== "place") return false;
"keepForLaterTooltip": "Your words are kept and nothing goes on the map; Save places it later",
findings.failure_scenario: A GM types the Final Truth's name, description and analysis, picks its room, presses New Remnant, answers 'Not now' as its tooltip invites, and comes back to an empty Final form.
findings.expected: docs/dev/e99/STATUS.md:670-671 says what the code does: 'Not now places nothing ... Its text fields without a room are not kept, as with Save.' The tooltip should say the form's words go with the window, or the reopened window should be handed them.

R6355 reviewed two other tooltips of the same family for saying what the code does; this one is listed only in tier 1's key census (tests-tier1.mjs:27910).

findings.title: A successful find of an undescribed trace waits on a window on the primary GM's browser alone, with no clock, card or second GM; a reload of that GM while it is open loses the find without a word
findings.where: scripts/observe.mjs:823 (scoreObserve awaits createFind before any result is written), 1030-1032 and 1183-1280 (describeFind: a window, awaited with no time), 751-756 (the mark `describing` lives in memory); scripts/bridge-table.mjs:132 (observe.resolve answers "ack")
findings.what_happens: An Observe that beats its number on a trace nobody has named opens describeFind on the GM that resolves it - the primary, for every player's Observe - and mints the bullet only when that window is answered or closed. The player's request was acknowledged when it arrived and says nothing more (for a General or Non-obvious sweep the roll card has no 'the GM is judging' line: action-observe.mjs:181). There is no card in the thread, no sound, no time on the window, and another GM is not shown it. If the primary reloads or leaves while it stands, the run dies with the page: the pending row is left with no result, nothing resolves it again, no bullet is made, no Sanity is taken and neither screen is told - the 'no record' whispers (observe.mjs:725-737) are for a resolve that arrives, and none does.
findings.failure_scenario: At a two-GM table the narrating GM is not the primary; a player's sweep succeeds, the window opens behind the other GM's map, and the player waits with a spent action and no card until somebody notices - or that GM presses F5 and the find is gone.
findings.expected: observe.mjs:978-980: 'a result that has already been rolled must never evaporate because a dialog was dismissed'; and the E09 C12 note (229-237) on the picker, the same shape: 'a second GM never learned the question existed, and a primary whose window was hidden left the player waiting out the whole clock'. The copy can be minted with the prefilled words at once and the description asked after, or the window given a time after which it answers as closed.
findings.fix_sketch: Mint first with the fallback words and ask the description afterwards (the trace's words reach the copy through setRemnantPublic), or end the window at TIMING.rulingMs as a close.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a clock or a second surface: describeFind is a drpgWindow with prompt true (stacking only; ui-kit.mjs has no sound), and nothing in call-gm.mjs holds an ask for it. Looked for a replay at ready: observe.mjs has only the TTL sweep; observe.resolve has no `resend` (bridge-table.mjs:123-138). A trace a GM named on the dashboard or the planner skips the window (1030-1031), so a prepared case meets it less; a trace an action left is unnamed until its first find (1010-1016).
findings.tests_near: tier 2 E51-T12/T13 close the window unanswered and read the copy; H84-02 reads the Reroll's refusal while a find is described. None reloads or times the window.
findings.live_check: Two GMs, a player sweeps a room with an unnamed trace and succeeds: note which GM gets the window and what the player's chat shows meanwhile; then reload the primary with the window open and read the player's sheet, Sanity and chat.

findings.title: observe.target takes `declaration` as sent and treats an unknown one as General, keeping the value on the GM's pending row for an hour; its claim says an unknown one is answered with a reason and never used
findings.where: scripts/bridge-table.mjs:111 and 114 (as.raw, and the claim); scripts/observe.mjs:271-283 (every value that is not followTraces, nonObvious or specific falls to the General shelf), 336-354 (pendObserve stores it), scripts/bridge-asks.mjs:825-826 (the same claim)
findings.what_happens: chooseObserveTarget compares the declaration with three of DECLARATIONS and sends anything else down the last branch, which picks the easiest trace as General does. The value itself - a string of any length, an object - is written into the pending entry and through to the observe store on the GM's browser, where it stays until the TTL sweep (TIMING.pendingObserveTtlMs, an hour). Nothing is gained over asking General, so this is dirt, not a gain: the claim R1b reads beside the field describes a check that is not there.
findings.failure_scenario: A console sends observe.target with declaration 'x': the GM answers a key for the easiest trace, and the pending row keeps 'x' (or whatever was sent) in the GM's browser storage for an hour.
findings.expected: The claim at bridge-table.mjs:114, or as.oneOf("general", "nonObvious", "followTraces", "specific") in the sanitizer with a refusal for anything else.
findings.fix_sketch: Sanitize with as.oneOf(...Object.values(DECLARATIONS)) and refuse a null.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for the comparison the claim names: DECLARATIONS is read at observe.mjs:188, 197, 228, 242, 282 and 382 only, none of which refuses. Bounds on packet text are put off to E43 by bridge-guards.mjs:1500-1502, which is why this is filed as dirt and a comment against code, not as a storage question.
findings.tests_near: 30-security and 33-bridge-paths send 'general' only; no test sends an unknown declaration (git grep).

by_decision.what: An Observe's declaration lives in the browser of the GM that minted it and is not exchanged between GMs; a resolve that reaches another GM finds no record and both screens are told, with no automatic refund.

by_decision.what: A GM's Refuse on a focused Observe's pick card does not give the action back: the roll already thrown goes to the GMs as a second card to rule on.
An Analyze refused by the GM keeps its price unless the refusal is a missing or unopened answer key.
A Key or a Final shows its kind at pickup and keeps its reading for an Analyze rolled against the Key column; a miss locks it for the chapter.
A critical find's hint is the finder's alone and is asked first in the describe window.
The dashboard's Save saves and closes; every other close writes the changed fields too, and a Final Truth with a room picked is asked about, never placed unasked.
by_decision.source: scripts/investigation.mjs:2423-2429 ('Nie, ma zapisywac', the owner, 13.11.2026), 2446-2456 (E24 C6, the owner, 09.11.2026); docs/dev/e99/STATUS.md:665-671

by_decision.what: Clear Faint and Collect the Truth Bullets have no button on the dashboard; End the chapter runs both.
An open Frisk's asks live in the primary GM's memory; a reload or a new primary ends them with no dice thrown and the action handed back.
A Frisk of a target the GMs alone know dead, or of a side of the running incident, plays as a living student who does not answer, its card's words to the GMs alone.

not_established: How often finding 1 happens at a table: it needs two finds of one unnamed trace inside one describe window's life. The live check under the finding settles the behaviour; a count of unnamed traces at the start of an Investigation in the owner's world would settle the frequency.

What one rebuild of `.drpg-case-live` costs with every node open: the window rebuilds on every updateActor, every item hook and six stores (investigation.mjs:2409-2418), debounced by TIMING.coalesceMs (120 ms), and the Map build runs allTraces over every scene, findersByAnyRemnant twice, layoutCase and a DOM measure of every node. live.mjs samples it (`live..drpg-case-live`, line 197); the number is game.drpg.perf()'s at a table and was not read here.

Whether Foundry v14 fires clientSettingChanged inside the awaited write of a client setting. observe.mjs:93-146 and gm-store.mjs:820-833 both rely on it (`pendingWriting`, `st.writing`). If it fired after, every own write would empty Observe's cache, and an entry held across the describe window would be written back without its result. Reading: log the order of the hook and the resolved promise on 14.370.

Whether a target's player on another browser tab notices an open Frisk's ask: frisk.ask opens a window with a 60-second clock and plays no sound (no sfx in frisk.mjs but the 'stolen' of a noticed hand). A table reading settles whether silence here is felt as a defect.

Whether a Reroll of an Observe can produce a bullet of a trace erased since the first throw: scoreObserve mints from the pending row's snapshot (entry.data, observe.mjs:983, 1104-1148) and createTruthBullet does not ask whether the trace still stands. The Reroll's own gates (reroll.mjs) were not read; a tier-2 probe that erases the trace between a miss and its Reroll would settle it.
